title: compact-onboard-pinwave-and-profile-publish-for-embed-rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add a compact onboarding flow that supports a single artifact that serves both embedding and pairwise reranker use-cases, enable an incremental "pinwave" version pinning process, and publish a lightweight performance profile bundle to the model catalog. This ticket covers engineering work to wire the canary rollout, update the profiling harness to capture latency/throughput/cost across realistic prefix distributions, and automate profile validation and publish steps.

Scope/Deliverables:
- Artifact ingestion adapter that accepts combined encoder+reranker bundles and validates compatibility with current kernel selection table.
- Pinwave flow: ability to create a pinned series (v1.0 -> v1.0.1 -> v1.1) with deterministic artifact naming and a promoted canary marker.
- Canary harness: k6-based traffic generator plus KV-cache priming script to exercise production-like prefixes.
- Profile format: a condensed JSON profile (<= 64KB) that records p50/p95 token latency, batch scaling curve, memory footprint, and recommended quantization knobs. Backward compatible with existing catalog consumers.
- Validation gates: unit + e2e checks including variability tests against the admission thresholds from ENG-42177 and cross-arch smoke tests.
- Automation: GitHub Actions pipeline to run the harness, produce profile artifacts, upload to the catalog, and create a release PR with diffs.

Important decisions and trade-offs considered:
- We opted for a compact profile schema to keep uploads small and enable quick comparisons in the Console, sacrificing some rare diagnostics (detailed kernel timings) which will remain available in full telemetry for debugging.
- Pinwave uses immutable artifact names and a lightweight canary marker rather than mutable pointers to make rollbacks deterministic across Dedicated and Private deployments. This increases storage of small artifact variants but simplifies routing/fallback logic.
- Canary sample size tuned conservatively to prioritize safety (higher p95 confidence) which may increase rollout time; will iterate if operations metrics show low variance.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-10: Initial spike complete. Prototype adapter that recognizes combined bundles and extracts both embedding and pairwise model configs. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Pinwave+Onboarding+Spike
- 2026-03-11: Added basic k6 harness and a KV priming utility. First-run profiles generated on a small G4 cluster. Artifact extractor PR opened.
- 2026-03-12: Integration review with runtime team. Requested changes: add cross-arch smoke test and ensure profile schema includes a top-level generation_seed field for reproducibility.
- 2026-03-13: Implemented smoke tests and generation_seed. Began wiring GH Actions pipeline; upload step targets internal catalog staging endpoint.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quantization recommendations in compact profile might be too aggressive for some workloads leading to quality regressions. Mitigation: Add a conservative fallback variant and require a short evaluation prompt-suite before auto-publish.
- Risk: Private deployments with strict storage quotas may object to additional artifact variants. Mitigation: provide a post-publish GC policy and optional delta-signing to reduce duplication.

Next steps / Checklist:
- Finalize profile JSON schema and publish docs (Confluence).
- Complete GH Actions end-to-end and flip staging->catalog endpoint.
- Run extended variability tests across x86 and arm pools (tracked in ENG-41002).
- Coordinate PM for canary rollout policy and add console UI hooks (PRD link below).

Links and artifacts:
- PR (prototype extractor): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Canary harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-harness/tree/compact-pinwave
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321
- Design notes for catalog UI: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C_pinwave_catalog_ui

Acceptance criteria:
- Combined artifact accepted by ingestion adapter without manual steps.
- Profile generation completes in <= 20 minutes on a standard test pool and produces a <=64KB profile file.
- GH Actions pipeline produces a catalog PR with profile and artifact metadata and triggers admission gates.
- Canary rollout completes with no regression above defined thresholds in p95 latency or quality for the evaluation prompt-suite.
